entry.title: Updated T2K measurement of neutrino oscillation parameters with the first data from the Gadolinium-loaded far detector
entry.summary: The T2K experiment presents updated measurements of neutrino oscillation parameters using $21.4(16.3)\times10^{20}$ protons on target (POT) in (anti-)neutrino mode at the far detector, Super-Kamiokande. This analysis uses an additional neutrino dataset of $1.7 \times 10^{20}$ POT compared to the previous result, and for the very first time, data collected with Super-Kamiokande doped with Gadolinium (Gd). Significant improvements were introduced in the far detector selection and systematic error treatment. Both semi-frequentist and Bayesian analyses are presented, including results on $\sin^{2} θ_{23}$, $Δm^2_{32} $, $\sin^{2} θ_{13}$ and $δ_{CP}$. Both analyses favor normal mass ordering with a nearly maximal CP-violating phase and are compatible with neutrino maximal mixing, slightly favouring the upper $θ_{23}$ octant.

entry.title: TeV-Scale Leptogenesis in the Linear Seesaw Framework
entry.summary: The linear seesaw mechanism relates the smallness of neutrino masses to the mass splitting within a quasi-Dirac pair of heavy neutrinos, thereby providing a natural framework for realising resonant leptogenesis at low energies. We investigate this possibility within its simplest effective realisation, in which neutrino masses are mediated by a quasi-Dirac pair at the TeV scale. We estimate the generation of the baryon asymmetry in the purely flavoured and strong-washout regimes, identifying phenomenologically viable parameter regions and benchmark scenarios in which the heavy-neutrino decays are dominated either by the SM Higgs doublet or by a second, leptophilic scalar doublet responsible for neutrino mass generation. We find viable leptogenesis solutions both near and away from the resonant maximum and discuss complementary phenomenological probes of the framework.

entry.title: On the effective atmospheric-scale $Δm^2$ in neutrino oscillation
entry.summary: We discuss an effective two-frequency description of the three-generation neutrino oscillation with the key quantity $Δm^2_{ \text{effective} }$, which unifies the effects of atmospheric-scale $Δm^2_{31}$-$Δm^2_{32}$ driven oscillations. As a solution to the minimization problem in vacuum, Nunokawa {\it et al.} obtained $Δm^2_{ \text{effective} } = Δm^2_{31} - (2E / L) \arctan \left\{ r_{2} \sin 2Δ_{21} / ( r_{1} + r_{2} \cos 2Δ_{21} ) \right\}$, where $Δ_{21} \equiv Δm^2_{21} L / (4 E)$ and $r_{i}$ are the mixing-angle dependent constants. Despite the skepticism for the $L/E$ dependence in this formula, we show, in fact, that this is an exact expression, which renders the probability formula also exact. We offer an appealing-to-intuition physical explanation for the $L/E$ dependence that it originates from the nature-designed three generation neutrinos. The way it is buried into $Δm^2_{ \text{effective} }$ is through the solar-effect renormalization to this quantity. With the physical interpretation of $Δm^2_{ \text{effective} }$ at hand, we aim at resolving the existing controversies on $Δm^2_{ \text{effective} }$ in this paper.

entry.title: Conditional multiparameter thermometry with neutrino oscillations: MSW energy diversity and a plasma-noise benchmark
entry.summary: We address temperature-parameter inference in a restricted two-flavor neutrino dephasing model with fixed mean electron densities. When two zone temperatures enter the propagated state via a single accumulated dephasing exponent, the single-energy quantum Fisher information matrix has rank at most 1. Independent, energy-resolved samples restore regular local identifiability when their thermal-sensitivity vectors are noncollinear. Matter-dependent mixing provides distinct weights in an illustrative two-zone model. A separate two-probe benchmark shows how complementary Bell sectors can distinguish temperature from spatial noise correlations. An electron-only Debye-cell estimate gives a conditional longitudinal quantum signal-to-noise ratio of approximately $3.1\times10^{-13}$ at 10 MeV for a uniform central-density medium over one solar radius. This estimate is not a microscopic upper bound or a detector sensitivity forecast. Complete phase averaging removes temperature information carried solely by longitudinal coherence damping; to retain solar sensitivity, a separate calculation of population, refractive, or production effects is required. entry.title: Light on GeV-scale seesaw
entry.summary: The next generation of beam-dump and accelerator-neutrino experiments will probe GeV-scale sterile neutrinos with unprecedented sensitivity. However, the tiny active-sterile mixing predicted by the minimal seesaw mechanism is expected to remain out of reach. Oscillation data require at least two sterile neutrinos, $N_1$ and $N_2$, which may couple to the photon through a transition dipole. Such a coupling can radically change the picture, both by strongly enhancing sterile-neutrino production and by opening new decay channels. We identify charged-lepton pairs produced by an off-shell photon as the most promising experimental signature. We show that the seesaw band can be probed by the T2K near detector for sterile-neutrino masses $m_N\lesssim 500$ MeV, and by SHiP for $m_N\lesssim 5$ GeV. For a sufficiently large dipole, $d\gtrsim (10~\mathrm{TeV})^{-1}$, SHiP can selectively measure decay channels that require nonzero active-sterile mixing. This would give rise to a distinctive hierarchy of signatures, providing a direct test of the seesaw mechanism.

entry.title: Fermionic dark linear seesaw with an anomalous Majoron
entry.summary: We propose a minimal fermionic realisation of the $\textit{dark}$ linear seesaw with spontaneous breaking of lepton number. The small lepton-number-violating parameter responsible for linear-seesaw neutrino masses is generated radiatively by a $\textit{dark}$ sector consisting of a singlet and a doublet fermion, together with scalar singlets. The global U(1)$_L$ symmetry is broken to a residual $\mathcal{Z}_2$ under which the $\textit{dark}$ sector is odd. This breaking yields a Majoron $J$ and makes the lightest $\textit{dark}$ particle stable. The charged $\textit{dark}$ fermion acquires its mass solely from U(1)$_L$ breaking and thus induces an anomalous Majoron coupling to photons. Current bounds on this coupling exclude a massless Majoron for TeV-scale U(1)$_L$ breaking. We add a linear term that breaks lepton number softly and gives the Majoron a GeV-scale mass. Such a Majoron decays into two photons and can be probed at beam-dump experiments. We study the dark matter phenomenology, focusing on the case where the stable particle is a fermionic weakly interacting massive particle. We analyse how the framework can be tested through charged-lepton flavour-violating decays such …

entry.title: Majorana Neutrino Exchange in Free-Baryon $B_1B_2\to ppe^-e^-$ Reactions
entry.summary: The free-baryon reactions $B_1B_2\to pp e^-e^-$ are studied for six nonstrange and strange initial states, with light- and heavy-Majorana-neutrino exchange treated in the same baryon-level framework. For light-neutrino exchange, the cross sections scale with the square of the effective Majorana mass $m_{ββ}$. The calculated cross sections increase as the off-shell cutoff $Δq^2$ is reduced, especially near threshold and in the hyperon channels, because more of the phase-space region where the squared four-momentum of the exchanged neutrino is close to zero is retained. At $\sqrt{s}=5.1~\mathrm{GeV}$, the six light-neutrino cross sections span $9.28\times10^{-49}$--$1.78\times10^{-45}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-2}$ for $m_{ββ}=30~\mathrm{meV}$ and $Δq^2=10^{-2}~\mathrm{GeV}^2$. For heavy-neutrino exchange, the cross sections scale with $η_N^2$, where $η_N=|U_{eN}|^2/m_N$. The leading propagator correction remains below one percent for $m_N\gtrsim50~\mathrm{GeV}$ over the phase-space region considered. At $\sqrt{s}=5.1~\mathrm{GeV}$, the heavy-neutrino cross sections span $7.55\times10^{-45}$--$1.98\times10^{-41}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-2}$ for $η_N=4.0\times10^{-9}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. At higher …

entry.title: Origin of flavour cancellations in thermal leptogenesis
entry.summary: In thermal leptogenesis with three hierarchical heavy neutrinos $N_1$, $N_2$ and $N_3$, the baryon asymmetry can be the small remainder of large contributions that cancel. Interference terms in the CP asymmetry are known to contribute to the final asymmetry through flavour-dependent washout. However, it remains unclear where the cancellation occurs, how large the interference contribution is, and how the accuracy of approximate equations changes when this information is lost. We split the CP asymmetry into diagonal and off-diagonal parts in the charged-lepton basis and evolve them with Standard Model transport equations. We find that the cancellation occurs mainly between the diagonal and off-diagonal parts of the same heavy neutrino, and that it is caused by flavour-dependent washout. We also find that the interference between the lepton state produced in the decay and the states orthogonal to it typically accounts for most of the $N_2$ and $N_3$ contribution. Approximations that reduce the CP asymmetry to flavour populations turn out to miss most of this contribution, whereas density-matrix equations with the full CP-asymmetry matrix agree much better.

entry.title: TeV Gamma-Ray Transparency Bounds on Neutrinos and Axions
entry.summary: Multi-TeV gamma rays propagating over cosmological distances measure the extragalactic background light (EBL) through attenuation by electron--positron pair production. This is particularly valuable in the infrared, where the EBL is difficult to measure directly. Since the growing sample of observed multi-TeV photons provides tight constraints on the EBL photon intensity, this, in turn, constrains new particles that radiatively decay into meV--eV photons. We set the first TeV-transparency bounds on active-neutrino electromagnetic transition moments, obtain new constraints on radiatively decaying sterile neutrinos, and derive competitive limits on the axion--photon coupling.

entry.title: Flavor Alignment and Operator Sensitivity in a Left--Right Universal-Seesaw Model
entry.summary: We analyse the flavour structure and low-energy operator sensitivity of a parity-related doublet universal-seesaw model with an imposed lepton triality. Degenerate bare singlet masses permit a basis in which light-light tree neutral flavour transitions vanish; the physical heavy masses remain nondegenerate. We connect this alignment property to the axial and scalar differences measured by $B_{d,s}^0\toμ^+μ^-$ and reproduce the six-state charged-vector mixing amplitudes for five reference masses. The reference analysis identifies kaon CP violation as the more sensitive flavour probe. Historical kaon data disfavour the lower reference masses, while estimates suggest that dimuon and radiative $B$-decay effects are harder to resolve at present precision. These comparisons use the specified reference spectrum and historical inputs. We also compare charged and neutral resonance rates with published search benchmarks. The vacuum hierarchy entails a cancellation of about $5\times10^{-6}$ at $M_{W_R}=80\,\mathrm{TeV}$. entry.title: Finite-temperature quark dynamics in proto-neutron stars: Maximum baryonic mass and radial oscillations
entry.summary: Finite-temperature quark dynamics can significantly alter proto-neutron star evolution even when the cold equation of state remains unchanged. We quantify this sensitivity by comparing a purely hadronic baseline with two hybrid models incorporating quark matter via the Polyakov-Nambu-Jona-Lasinio (PNJL) framework and its entanglement extension (EPNJL), which isolates the role of finite-temperature chiral-deconfinement coupling. Employing bulk Gibbs constructions for both nuclear liquid-gas and hadron-quark phase coexistence, we compute equilibrium configurations across hot neutrino-trapped, hot neutrino-free, and cold stages, alongside linear radial oscillations of selected hot neutrino-free stars. Introducing quarks lowers the maximum baryonic mass at every stage and reverses its evolutionary ordering: whereas the maximum baryonic mass increases toward the cold limit in the purely hadronic model, it decreases progressively in both hybrid models, opening mass windows for delayed collapse. Crucially, despite sharing the same cold limit, PNJL and EPNJL yield distinct baryonic-mass intervals for mixed-core survival across stages: only EPNJL permits configurations that retain mixed …

entry.title: Measuring the flavor composition of high-energy neutrinos from the Milky Way
entry.summary: The origin of the Milky Way's high-energy neutrinos is debated. Their flavor composition reflects how they are made and could help settle it, but remains to be measured. We show that IceCube and KM3NeT, which see the inner Galaxy in complementary ways from opposite hemispheres, could start resolving its flavor composition in about a decade. With upcoming telescopes, they would infer the $ν_e$ fraction at the sources to within 27%. A first comparison of Galactic and extragalactic flavor compositions could reveal strong magnetic fields in extragalactic sources or neutrino decay.

entry.title: Confronting $b \to (s, d)μ^+ μ^-$ and $\mathcal{L}_{K^{*}\bar{K}^{*}}$ puzzle in a $U(1)_{B-3L_μ}$ framework with neutrino phenomenology
entry.summary: Current data on several observables in $b \to (s,d)$ $μ^+ μ^-$ transitions reveal certain discrepancies with Standard Model (SM) predictions. Considering the possibility that these deviations stem from new physics, we explore a $Z^{\prime}$ framework based on $U(1)_{B-3L_μ}$ model. The parameter space is examined in light of existing constraints from $b \to (s,d)$ $μ^+ μ^-$ transitions. Within this framework, we show that the quark couplings accommodating $b \to (s,d)$ $μ^+ μ^-$ anomalies, imprint correlated signatures on the non-leptonic puzzles $\mathcal{L}_{K^{*}\bar{K}^{*}}$ in $B_{s(d)} \to K^{*}\bar{K}^{*}$ decays. We find that the scenario with both vector and axial-vector contributions of opposite sign is favored by the data compared to pure vector contribution, offering a correlated probe of the underlying new-physics scenario. We further explore the neutrino phenomenology within the same framework in light of current data.

entry.title: Lower Bound on the Lightest Neutrino Mass with Resonant Neutrino Self-Interactions
entry.summary: We show the possibility of using the resonant $s$-channel scattering of ultra high energy astrophysical neutrinos with the low energy cosmic neutrino background to put a lower bound on the lightest neutrino mass. This can be realized and illustrated by neutrino self-interactions with a light scalar mediator of $\mathcal O(1)$ MeV mass. After analyzing the kinematics and cross section features of the $s$-channel resonance, we derive from first principles the double transport equations with double regeneration terms for the coupled evolution of neutrinos and anti-neutrinos. The simulated event spectrum is then compared with the HESE 7.5 year data observed at IceCube to give a clear lower bound on the lightest neutrino mass.

entry.title: Collisional dynamics of neutrino flavor conversion: angular structures, inhomogeneity, and decoherence
entry.summary: Self-interacting neutrino gases exhibit collective behavior, in which additional incoherent collisions can induce collisional neutrino-flavor instability. We investigate the effects of energy dependence, anisotropy, and spatial inhomogeneity on the resulting flavor conversion through linear stability analysis and nonlinear quantum kinetic simulations. We find contrasting wavenumber dependences for the near/gapless and far/gapped branches, with maximum growth rates at collision-scale shifted wavenumbers and at collective-scale wavenumbers, respectively. Their eigenvectors reveal distinct energy and angular structures, which are reflected in the subsequent establishment of flavor swap and equipartition. The nonlinear evolution also features secondary flavor growth associated with changes in the stability of collective modes as the neutrino background evolves. Despite the spreading of flavor coherence across spatial scales due to nonlinear mode coupling, collisional decoherence tends to limit the development of spatial inhomogeneities, leaving the neutrino populations nearly homogeneous. These findings represent a step towards understanding and predicting the nonlinear flavor …

entry.title: NuSrcAgent: An AI Agent for High-Energy Neutrino Source Searches
entry.summary: Identifying the sources of high-energy cosmic neutrinos is crucial for understanding cosmic particle accelerators and probing new physics. IceCube provides public data that allow researchers to search independently for neutrino sources, but these analyses require substantial technical expertise and careful scientific choices. We present \system, the first publicly available AI agent for high-energy neutrino source searches. Compared to public likelihood codes, \system is easier to install and use, and supports more analysis types. To start an analysis, users need only specify a source or catalog. The agent takes natural-language requests, runs likelihood analyses on public IceCube event data, and saves the settings and calculation records so users can repeat the analyses. We demonstrate \system through single-source and catalog stacking analyses, obtaining results consistent with IceCube results.
